audits.claim: The new assignment_source argument on the abstract status-sync method is unused by the status-sync call path.
audits.evidence: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411-418 adds an optional assignment_source argument, but src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:19,43-46 neither accepts a source nor passes one to should_sync or sync_status_outbound. The source-aware gate at mixins/issues.py:390-391 therefore cannot suppress status syncing based on that argument, whereas the assignee task explicitly reconstructs and passes the source at src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-60. This confirms an unused abstract API parameter; it does not establish a newly introduced status-sync loop, since the status path is unchanged and no status-cycle guarantee is documented by this method.

audits.claim: The tests omit both a different-integration source that must still sync outbound and an assertion that inbound syncing propagates its source.
audits.evidence: tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:179-221 supplies a matching AssignmentSource and checks that outbound synchronization is skipped, while :149-162 tests successful outbound synchronization only with assignment_source=None. Repository-wide searches for AssignmentSource and assignment_source in tests find no different-ID source test; the inbound tests at :321-347 and :378-388 assert assignment state without inspecting the propagated source or outbound suppression. The implementation does pass a source on both inbound branches at src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:94-99,112-116, and mixins/issues.py:390-394 permits a different ID when configured, so the finding identifies missing regression coverage rather than incorrect current behavior.
